principles: Treat current inventory N as immutable denominator for each kickoff epoch; execute plus admissible reuse must cover all rows.
Derive authoritative triggers from certified source closures and dual-revision graphs; manual declarations only add coverage.
Fail closed on uncertainty and preserve complete full validation as fallback, periodic baseline, and audit oracle.
Separate selection width, scheduler latency, internal sharding, focused validation, and DONE-required authority.
Make every gate-consumed fact signed, digest-bound, ancestry-compatible, clean-tree generated, current, and mechanically verifiable.
drivers: Reduce routine validation latency without weakening deterministic TEST/DONE assurance.
Eliminate false-negative reuse routes from incomplete triggers, stale dist, deleted/renamed paths, cross-branch receipts, and ambiguous lookup.
Give operators an exact reason for every execute/reuse/escalation decision.
Support staged observe, shadow, and low-risk enforcement with rollback.

options.name: Heuristic path filter
cons: Contradicts the approved plan and gate authority

options.name: Atomic all-at-once replacement
cons: No equivalence evidence before authority changes
Hard to isolate receipt, graph, gate, scheduler, and shard failures

options.name: Phased proof-carrying program
pros: Matches DYN-1 through DYN-5 and audit gates
Full oracle remains authoritative until soundness evidence exists
Each receipt, closure, selection, gate, schedule, and shard invariant is independently testable
cons: Requires current-main discovery and durable evidence campaigns before enforcement
Initial warm/cold graph and baseline overhead must be measured

rationale: The approved design explicitly requires observe-only catalog/closure/selection first, per-command receipt shadow reuse second, narrowly admitted low-risk TEST authority third, then scheduler and shard optimizations. This is the only option that preserves the complete inventory denominator and makes false-negative, stale receipt, scope, ancestry, build, revocation, and full-only failures fail closed before authority changes.

preMortem.scenario: A missing static, runtime, or process-fact edge leaves a changed command in reuse and a full run later fails.
preMortem.trigger: Fault injection or historical replay observes a full failure outside the dynamic execute set, or a trace path is outside the certificate.
preMortem.consequence: Dynamic authority could claim a false PASS.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep DYN-1 observe/shadow full oracle authoritative; invalidate incomplete certificates; require FI-1/FI-5 and zero false negatives before DYN-3.

preMortem.scenario: A stale pre-build dist or cross-branch receipt is accepted because digest fields happen to match.
preMortem.trigger: Build output changes after provisional planning, sourceHead is not a trusted ancestor, baseline epoch drifts, or receipt is expired/revoked/dirty.
preMortem.consequence: A command is reused without current source or environment proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Always execute Wave 0 source-first build; bind buildProofDigest, ancestry, epoch, clean-tree, expiry, and revocation ledger into receipt and TEST gate.

preMortem.scenario: A gate or catalog change is misclassified as low-risk and dynamic authority bypasses full validation.
preMortem.trigger: Protected/explicit-exclusion path, lifecycle/process/runtime fact, selector/executor/scheduler/catalog, package/config, or unmapped path changes.
preMortem.consequence: Shared validation semantics change without complete-plan verification.
preMortem.mitigation: Maintain mandatory full escalation classifier and blocking Section 24 prerequisites; reject missing catalog ownership and ignored escalation.

preMortem.scenario: Weighted scheduling or sharding changes verdicts, omits a case, or leaves residue.
preMortem.trigger: CPU weight removal, resource claim mutation, missing drain barrier, deleted/duplicated/wrong-routed shard, or static PASS sentinel.
preMortem.consequence: A faster report hides incomplete or contaminated validation.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep scheduler/shard work after authority proof; retain serial/full equivalence, stable sentinels, exact aggregation, mutation matrix, and zero residue checks.

preMortem.scenario: The program claims a universal latency SLA from favorable runs while full-escalated or heavy domains remain slow.
preMortem.trigger: Performance report excludes full escalation or quorum/review-pass population and uses best-run instead of paired medians.
preMortem.consequence: Operators lose an honest expectation and may disable safety controls.
preMortem.mitigation: Report risk-tier populations, warm/cold selection overhead, medians/P75, and full-escalated domains separately; do not claim 12–14 minutes universally.
